rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is nonexistent, so this experiment tests the effectiveness of a multimodal approach with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, and weighted fusion. It clarifies whether multimodal integration improves performance compared to rna-only baselines, addressing the primary objective of validation accuracy while isolating key design choices.

The existing evidence shows that config_002 (multimodal, singleprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, no aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves 0.537 validation accuracy. This experiment tests changing the image encoder from imagenet_vit_l to resnet50 while keeping other parameters identical, isolating the effect of the image encoder choice. This clarifies whether the image encoder significantly impacts performance, a critical design decision. It balances exploration (testing a different encoder) with exploitation (building on the existing multimodal setup).

The existing evidence shows that using resnet50 as the image encoder (config_023) slightly outperforms imagenet_vit_l (config_002). This experiment tests the impact of switching to multiprofile setting with the same RNA (scvi_n200) and image (resnet50) encoders used in config_023, but with aggregation None and fusion concat. This isolates the effect of the profile setting change, which is critical for determining if multiprofile configurations can improve performance. It balances exploration of a key design choice (profile setting) while leveraging existing evidence about encoder effectiveness.

Existing evidence shows that resnet50 image encoders (config_023) slightly outperform imagenet_vit_l (config_002) in singleprofile setups, while weighted fusion (config_002) is better than concat (config_021). This experiment tests multiprofile (untested in previous top performers) with resnet50 (best image encoder so far), transformer aggregation (more effective than avgpool in some contexts), and weighted fusion (proven better in singleprofile). It isolates the impact of multiprofile settings and aggregation methods, which are critical design choices with sparse prior evidence.

Existing evidence shows config_010 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000 RNA, resnet50 image, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest validation accuracy (0.5729). This experiment tests whether replacing resnet50 with imagenet_vit_l as the image encoder could further improve performance, isolating the impact of the image encoder choice. It is the best next step because it directly evaluates a critical design decision (image encoder) while keeping other parameters consistent with the current top performer, maximizing information gain with minimal parameter changes.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile settings with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_005) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder to scgpt (a more complex model) while keeping the top-performing aggregation/fusion setup improves performance. It isolates the impact of the RNA encoder choice, a critical design decision with sparse prior evidence, and leverages the strong foundation of the current best configuration.

Existing evidence shows that config_005 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, transformer agg, concat fusion) achieves the highest validation accuracy (0.585594). This experiment tests changing the image encoder from imagenet_vit_l to resnet50 while keeping RNA encoder, aggregation, and fusion type the same. This isolates the effect of the image encoder choice, which is critical for determining whether the current top performer's image encoder is optimal. It balances exploitation of the high-performing multiprofile setup with exploration of a key design choice.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_005) achieve high accuracy (0.5856). This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (while keeping other components identical) improves performance, isolating the impact of RNA representation choice. This directly addresses a key design decision with potential to improve accuracy.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_045) achieve the highest accuracy. This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder (scvi_n200 → scgpt) in config_045's setup improves performance, isolating the impact of the RNA encoder choice. It balances exploitation of the high-performing transformer/weighted fusion framework with exploration of critical design decisions.

Existing evidence shows that config_045 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieves the highest validation accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from weighted to concat (while keeping other parameters identical) impacts performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. This comparison is critical to determine if the current best model's success hinges on weighted fusion, which could guide future optimizations.
